clue.text: I'm cast — miscast — as a joiner

indicators.note: to miscast is to cast wrongly, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor protests at being given the wrong part, that of a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscast' shuffles IMCAST, the letters of 'I'm cast', into a word for an adhesive; 'as a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin cement used to bond or seal materials, so it joins things together.

clue.text: He's unlikely to suffer from hives

definitions.text: He's unlikely to suffer from hives

parts.words: He's unlikely to suffer from hives
parts.note: hives is read not as the skin rash but as the homes of bees, which this person tends without fuss

explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper keeps bees in hives, so lives among them rather than suffering a rash.

clue.text: Part of church where pattern's irregular

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of the word beside it are out of order

explanation.surface: A part of a church is noted for its uneven floor pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges PATTERNS, the possessive treated as plain S; 'where' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross arm of a cruciform church building.

clue.text: Conservative support rising with relation to something precious

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
an uncle is a relation

explanation.surface: A Tory backs a relative who is connected to some treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BRA up to ARB in this down entry; 'with' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gem such as a garnet, a valued stone.

clue.text: Tree needs steady treatment in an emergency

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
staid means sober and steady

explanation.surface: A felled tree calls for calm, steady handling in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic medical care given at once at an accident scene, before professional help arrives.

clue.text: Clerk I fired used to be lax as a Bradford note-writer

indicators.note: lax means loose, so these letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: An employer explains sacking a careless clerk from a Bradford firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be lax' rearranges CLERKIFIREDUSED; 'as a' is link. The composer Delius was born in Bradford, a Yorkshire city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delius, the English composer born in Bradford, wrote music, which is notes on paper.

clue.text: Groom turns up to catch sheep

indicators.note: turns up, in a down entry, says the joined words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net is to catch
rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: A stable hand arrives in time to catch some sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses NETRAMS as a whole; 'to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy someone's appearance, to make neat.

clue.text: Advance to shoot at the flag

definitions.meaning: to advance is to come nearer
in golf, the shot played towards the flag on the green

explanation.surface: Instructions to move forward and fire at a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is link. The second sense is golfing: the flag marks the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance toward something is to come near; in golf the stroke onto the green is this shot.

clue.text: In Irish city is nothing laughable?

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the city's name

parts.note: Derry is a city in Northern Ireland
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Asking whether anything in an Irish city is funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, not a link word: the city's name is split open after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or poor as to deserve ridicule, ridiculous.

clue.text: Differential is geared to differ

indicators.note: differential suggests something made different, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car's differential gear is described as being built to make wheels turn at different speeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Differential' looks like car engineering but signals an anagram of ISGEARED; 'to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at odds in opinion is to differ, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: McNeile's an engineer

definitions.meaning: H. C. McNeile, creator of Bulldog Drummond, wrote under this pen name; 's here means is
a soldier of the Royal Engineers, who digs saps or trenches

explanation.surface: A writer is said to have had a career in engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: McNeile served in the Royal Engineers and took the soldiers' nickname as his pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of the thriller writer H. C. McNeile, and also the term for a military engineer who builds field works.

clue.text: Soft comfort, not a constraint

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be removed from the word just given

parts.note: to comfort is to reassure

explanation.surface: A soft cushion is said to be a comfort rather than a restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft' looks like a description of the cushion but is the musical P; 'not a' removes just one A from the comforting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is force or compulsion bearing on someone, a kind of restraint.

clue.text: Gets an edge but game's over

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read from its end back to its start

parts.note: games, taken as a plural, are sports

explanation.surface: Someone gains an advantage but the match has already ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SPORTS round; 'but' is link. Stropping a razor on a leather strap sharpens it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop is to hone a blade on a leather strap, giving it a keen cutting side.

clue.text: With all the cards I can finish

parts.note: a full pack is all the cards in a deck
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A card player holding every card claims the game is won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is link. PACK IT IN is a British idiom for stopping or giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: to stop doing something or give up is to quit, the same as to end it.

clue.text: Turn India blue? That's unheard-of!

definitions.note: read as un-heard of, describing something not heard

indicators.note: turn says the letters are turned around into another order

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to the suggestion of painting India blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges INDIABLUE. 'unheard-of' normally means unprecedented, but split as un-heard it means not able to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully as not-heard, it means too quiet for the ear to pick up.

clue.text: In haste to withdraw an amendment

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a rush, someone backs away from a proposed change.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is found across 'haste to'. Proofreaders write the Latin 'let it stand' to cancel a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, cancelling a correction already marked.

clue.text: Get up and enter knobbly knees competition

definitions.meaning: a dated idiom telling someone to get out of bed
at a holiday camp contestants display their legs to be judged

explanation.surface: A summer-camp host urging people out of bed to join a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Knobbly knees contests were a British holiday-camp tradition where men bared their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old call to rise from bed, and literally means displaying one's leg, as in a knees contest.

clue.text: Hiding source of belladonna, something that gives out poison

indicators.note: hiding says the word for a giver-out conceals another letter

parts.note: an emitter is a thing that gives out light or radiation

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Belladonna, deadly nightshade, is concealed, being something that releases poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' puts B, the first letter from 'source of belladonna', inside EMITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter is to sour feelings, to poison them figuratively.

clue.text: Hail a boat

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel or barge

explanation.surface: Flag down a passing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's call used to greet or attract a ship, as a shouted greeting.

clue.text: Charming party in cultivated surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the word for cultivated encloses the party

parts.note: arable land is cultivated, ploughed and farmed
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A delightful party held amid well-tended grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is link; 'surroundings' is the container signal, with farmland wrapped round the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean delightful and lovable, synonyms.

clue.text: Guns, not one in order

indicators.note: not says the numeral is to be removed from the decree

parts.note: an ordinance is a decree or official order
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Weapons are said to be out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' takes I out of ORDINANCE; 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery, the big weapons of an army.

clue.text: Salt to dress bananas

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or dress up
a hand is a bunch of bananas

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting a coating on fruit with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is the definition, an old sea sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor; a deckhand is a sailor working on deck.

clue.text: Arrange to pass on concealed bribes upwards

indicators.note: concealed says the reversed bribes are hidden inside the word for pass on

parts.note: to pass on is to die

indicators.note: upwards, in a down entry, says the word for bribes is read backwards

parts.note: sops are bribes given to pacify

explanation.surface: Someone sets things up to hand on bribes kept hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' turns SOPS to SPOS; 'concealed' sets it in DIE, as DI-SPOS-E. 'to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose is to place things in order, to arrange them.

clue.text: Fancy listening to Lord Peter!

indicators.note: listening to says we want a word heard, not seen, matching the surname

parts.note: Lord Peter Wimsey is Dorothy L. Sayers's aristocratic detective

explanation.surface: Imagine hearing the famous detective himself speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a whim or capricious notion, a playful idea.

clue.text: Being a stayer, you are, we hear, in the final

indicators.note: in puts the spoken letters inside the word for the final part

parts.note: the ending is the final part

indicators.note: we hear says letters are chosen to match the spoken words

parts.note: said quickly these two words sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: A stamina runner is told they have made it through to the last race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'you are' into the letters UR, which go 'in' ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting or persisting over time stays the course, hence lasts.

clue.text: Preparation to apply for auction's opening and closing items

annotationWithheld.clue: Preparation to apply for auction's opening and closing items

clue.text: I am grown up, standing outside wine store and drinking

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: standing outside says the word for grown up surrounds the wine store

parts.note: big means grown up, adult
a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles

explanation.surface: An adult stands outside a wine merchant while having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing outside' is the container signal; the wine store goes after the second letter of the grown-up word. 'and' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbibing is drinking, especially alcohol, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Grand Canyon, the heart of bucolic America

parts.note: a canyon is a deep gorge

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: The Grand Canyon is praised as the centre of rural American scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like part of the canyon's name; it is the definition, in its sense of splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something splendid and magnificent in appearance.

clue.text: Still behind the Spanish team

indicators.note: behind puts the word for still after the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
still can mean even, as in even better

explanation.surface: A Spanish side is still trailing.
explanation.walkthrough: Football and cricket sides each have this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this number of players, so the number names the side.
